gaps.sentence: ___, I'd like to thank the volunteers who worked behind the scenes.
gaps.explanation: 'Finally' introduces the last point of a list or speech.

gaps.sentence: ___ you finish early, come and give us a hand.
gaps.explanation: 'If' introduces a real condition; 'in case' would change the meaning to precaution.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: ___ the north coast is rocky, the southern beaches are soft golden sand.
gaps.explanation: 'While' can contrast two clauses in a single sentence.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: ___ had I closed my eyes than the alarm went off.
gaps.explanation: The 'than' in the sentence forces 'No sooner', the only linker paired with than.
